notesStmt.note: This proof slip was almost certainly printed prior to the poem's first publication, as another copy (hun.00015) shows evidence of having been annotated sometime between May 1885 and November 1887. The specific handwritten changes on this proof slip were never incorporated into any of the published versions of the poem, nor did the poem appear in a final position, as per the note at the top. It is possible, therefore, that the handwritten portions reflect ideas that Whitman entertained but abandoned as he worked, in 1888, to incorporate the "Sands at Seventy" poems into subsequent printings of Leaves of Grass.

"You Lingering Sparse Leaves of Me" was first published in the November 1887 issue of Lippincott's Magazine. There, the poem was part of a four-poem sequence titled "November Boughs." That grouping was not maintained when the poem was further revised and printed in November Boughs (1888) and in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891-1892).

body.head:
YOU LINGERING SPARSE LEAVES
OF ME.

lg.l: You lingering sparse leaves of me on bare December?November boughs,
And I some well-shorn tree of field or orchard-row;

You tokens diminute and lorn—(not now the flush of May,—
nor July clover bloom, —no fruits of August now;)

You pallid little banners, remnants valueless—you overstay'd
of time,
Yet my soul-dearest leaves—the hardiest and the last.
